newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore CyberWay expands international network.
newsitem.headline: Singapore CyberWay expands international network.

text.p: CyberWay Pte Ltd, one of Singapore's three internet access providers, said on Tuesday it has expanded its international network to allow subscribers faster access to global internet destinations.

The company, a joint venture between Singapore Press Holdings and Singapore Technologies Pte Ltd, said it has doubled its data carrying capacity between Singapore and the U.S. with a second line, set up at an operating cost of Singapore $1.3 million a year.
It said a new connection, jointly set up with Hong Kong Telecom IMS, has been set up to carry internet traffic between Singapore and Hong Kong.

CyberWay has also expanded its roaming service beyond the U.S., Japan, Taiwan and Hong Kong into Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand. It expects to add South Korea, China, the United Kingdom, Canada, Switzerland and Australia into the service by first quarter 1997.
